newsitem.title: MALTA: Lombard Malta makes record profit.
newsitem.headline: Lombard Malta makes record profit.

text.p: Lombard Bank (Malta) saw pre-tax profits rise by a record 47 percent to Lm553,271 ($1.5 million) in the year ending September 30, bank chairman Albert Muscat told a shareholders' meeting late on Wednesday.
He said the bank's balance sheet grew by 74 percent compared to the previous financial year, so that total assets under management reached Lm79 million.
Loans and advances to customers went up by 27.5 percent to almost Lm21 million. Customers' deposits grew by 83 percent, including a 33 percent increase in local deposits.
As at September 30 net asset value per share stood at Lm1.18, up by 7.3 percent over the previous year.
Profit before tax on shareholders' funds increased from 11.3 percent in September, 1995 to 15.6 percent. Earnings per share rose from 10.5c to 12.3c.
"These results were due to the clear and defined strategies implemented by the bank, helping to ensure a focused and disciplined approach in the management of its business." Muscat said.
Lombard Bank (Malta) is one of Malta's smallest banks, with a headquarters and three branches. It was privatised three years ago and listed on the Malta Stock Exchange.
